reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of Hebrew people actively expressing their views and concerns. Moses and Aaron explicitly communicate God's command to Pharaoh, stating their position clearly. The Hebrew supervisors and officers (שֹׁטְרֵי בְנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) cry out to Pharaoh (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה) and directly express their grievances about working conditions. The people themselves voice their concerns about needing to leave to worship God. Far from being discouraged from expressing their views, the text shows them repeatedly voicing their positions, complaints, and religious convictions despite facing harsh oppression and increased labor demands.
